summary: floor returns the greatest integer less than or equal to a real value.
documentation: floor returns the greatest integer less than or equal to a real value. It moves toward negative infinity, which differs from truncation toward zero for negative numbers.
inputs: A real number or an object implementing the floor protocol.
caution: int(float_value) truncates rather than floors. Do not substitute it when negative inputs are meaningful.
scenarios: Find the lower integer boundary of a measurement interval.
Assign a signed position to a unit-width numeric bin.
Compute completed units under an explicitly downward rounding rule.
title: Find the lower integer boundary
problem: Input is a finite number. Return its mathematical floor. In particular, -2.3 becomes -3. Tests avoid ambiguous floating-point boundaries.
goal: Use math.floor() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Import math and call floor, rather than int.
